scope: Finish the Map sender/receiver of routed secondary-party monster EXP/hunt rewards and load native monster hunt grouping. Inherited C++ and SQL are implementation references, not independent certification of Gameforge balance.

history_review.finding: Party rewards originally mutate every local copy; remote branch and monster wKind were omitted.
Preserve local WithExpBonus, soulmate distribution and level-up World notification.
Preserve level 140, EXP saturation and soul-bar overflow guards; GainExp is unchanged.
Retain shared party money/access checks and existing gameplay integrity fixes.
Append hunt kind without shifting prior monster columns, skill slots, recall/tame fields or constructor defaults.

references.rule: Split nearby party shares by level, award bonuses/soulmate locally only for main copies; secondary copies relay base EXP and the wKind hunt event with monster position.
Validate current main character/key, apply EXP then CheckQuest with the carried term/position/count.
Native GainExp suppresses monster experience for a dead character.
Existing receiver-key route and verbatim body reframing are unchanged.

implemented: Secondary nearby party copies relay their computed share and hunt event to World; they do not mutate their local EXP or quest state. Nearby party count/share arithmetic remains unchanged.
Map receives the existing World route on a current main InGame session/key; player-port injection and stale/loading/secondary routes cannot grant rewards.

Receiver uses already-scaled EXP without applying local premium/buff/soulmate distribution again. Existing level cap, saturation, level-up heal and soul-bar logic are reused; dead recipients do not gain EXP or revive.

TMONSTERCHART.wKind now supplies hunt objective IDs for local and routed kills. Real zero values are preserved; synthetic templates with no kind retain chart-ID fallback. Local hunt triggers use the monster kill position.

validation.platform: Isolated Linux .NET 10 SDK, source read-only. General DB suites gated; only the named hunt-kind test ran against live SQL.

remaining: Real-client multi-Map topology, party rewards, quest persistence and logout/restart require verification. This does not enable an otherwise missing distributed topology.
Native wKind values come from inherited SQL and still require independent reference-content verification. No probabilities or balance values were invented.
The separate native party-quest-once flag and QTT_SPAWNID_DEL proximity branch remain outside this slice. Existing local party quest policy was retained.
World reward messages have no native event nonce; this port does not invent deduplication that could drop legitimate respawn kills.
follow_up: Gameforge/quest-engine.json ports the local party-once Regen flag, type-21 proximity and routed Regen death coordinates; the remaining list above describes this earlier slice.

current_deployment.note: Earlier implementation/validation notes retain their historical scope. Current cumulative source is deployed; deployment does not certify whole-game or full gameplay restart parity.
